text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.
LONDON - British shares closed higher on Wednesday, near the best levels of the day as the stock market was revived by renewed takeover activity and sentiment improved on Wall Street.
The FTSE 100 index finished 38.6 points better at 4,018.2, regaining the 4,000 level for the first time in five days.
News that U.S. group Entergy Corp had made an agreed 1.267 billion stg bid for London Electricity helped UK shares get off to a positive start.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse dealings with modest gains on Wednesday, encouraged by overnight gains on Wall Street and supported by a firmer dollar. The DAX index of 30 top German shares closed up 5.62 points at 2,820.75. Dealers said news of weaker-than-expected November German M3 money supply growth of eight percent released in the morning had also been supportive for the market. In post-bourse trade the index rose 5.73 to 2,814.23.

PARIS - French shares held on to their gains to close higher on Wednesday, supported by strength on Wall Street, and traders were moderately hopeful about further progress. "If New York finishes higher, if the dollar holds steady in around 5.25 francs and rates stay steady, we have the grounds to move a bit higher," said one. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 25.19 points at 2,218.89.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed firmer but below the day's highs, only just failing to break resistance around 3,875 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI). Trading volume rose in the second half. Short covering ahead of Friday's expiry on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) as well as a friendly beginning on Wall Street buoyed Swiss shares, a dealer said. The all share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 11.73 points to 2,471.62.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks fell sharply in thin trade on Wednesday but the benchmark Nikkei average finished above the 20,000 level. Brokers said the fall was triggered by speculative futures sales, adding that the feeble sentiment may linger for a while. The Nikkei 225 average ended down 320.43 points at 20,093.03, the day's low.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed on a weaker note on Wednesday, led down by losses in the property sector as a lack of incentives prevented share prices from retaining some early gains. The Hang Seng Index shed 49.35 points to 12,766.02 after rising to a session high of 12,942.63.
SYDNEY - Australian shares finished a quiet session modestly firmer on Wednesday with stocks holding on to early gains after Wall Street hinted that its recent rally was not yet complete.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 7.9 points higher at 2,323.7, not far from its intra-day high of 2,328.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks ended a volatile day firmly up on Wednesday as buyers returned to a battered market after a heavy sell-off on Tuesday related to the close-out of the December futures contract, dealers said. Shares started up, boosted by strong gains from Wall Street overnight, but took a knock by noon as futures-related selling kicked in.

However, more positive sentiment began to seep through the market in the afternoon and underlying institutional demand returned, giving stock prices a final leg up in a hectic rush of late trade. The all-share index ended at 6,414.9, up 30.9 points, as industrials rose 66.2 points to close at 7,635.1. The gold index finished up 11.0 points at 1,488.7.
